ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A circuit and the characteristics of the diode \(D\) in it are shown in the figure. The ratio of the minimum to the maximum small-signal voltage gain \(\frac{\partial V_{\text{out}}}{\partial V_{\text{in}}}\) is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a circuit; the input voltage Vin is connected through a 2 kΩ resistor to the middle node, which is labeled Vout. The Vout node is then connected through a 2 kΩ resistor to the right-side node, and the right-side node is connected through a vertical 2 kΩ resistor to the bottom reference node. Diode D is connected between the Vout node and the right-side node, forming a parallel path with the upper 2 kΩ resistor. On the right side, the diode characteristic is given: before about 0.7 V the current is zero, and after conduction the characteristic is approximately vertical, so the small-signal equivalent has two states: open circuit when off, and approximately short circuit when on. Reasoning: In the small-signal state where the diode is off, replace D with an open circuit. At this time, the load looking from Vout toward ground is the series connection of the two right-side 2 kΩ resistors, namely 2 kΩ + 2 kΩ = 4 kΩ. Therefore the voltage-divider gain is Vout/Vin = 4/(2 + 4) = 2/3. In the small-signal state where the diode is on, replace D with a short circuit; it shorts Vout and the right-side node, and also equivalently shorts the 2 kΩ resistor between the two nodes. At this time, from Vout to ground only the vertical 2 kΩ resistor remains as the load, so the voltage-divider gain is Vout/Vin = 2/(2 + 2) = 1/2. The minimum gain is 1/2 and the maximum gain is 2/3, so the required ratio is (1/2)/(2/3) = 3/4 = 0.75.

raw_record.question_text: A circuit and the characteristics of the diode \(D\) in it are shown in the figure. The ratio of the minimum to the maximum small-signal voltage gain \(\frac{\partial V_{\text{out}}}{\partial V_{\text{in}}}\) is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image and identify the two diode operating regions from the plotted characteristic. In the diode-off small-signal state, replace D by an open circuit; the load seen from Vout is the series combination 2 kΩ + 2 kΩ = 4 kΩ, so compute the divider gain Vout/Vin = 4/(2+4) = 2/3. In the diode-on small-signal state, replace D by a short circuit across the 2 kΩ resistor between Vout and the right node; the load becomes only the vertical 2 kΩ resistor, so compute the divider gain Vout/Vin = 2/(2+2) = 1/2. Take the ratio of the smaller gain to the larger gain: (1/2)/(2/3) = 0.75.

图像描述：图中左侧是电路，输入电压 Vin 通过一个 2 kΩ 电阻接到中间节点，该节点标为 Vout。Vout 节点再通过一个 2 kΩ 电阻接到右侧节点，右侧节点通过一个竖直的 2 kΩ 电阻接到底部参考节点。二极管 D 连接在 Vout 节点与右侧节点之间，与上方的 2 kΩ 电阻形成并联通路。右侧给出了二极管特性：在约 0.7 V 之前电流为零，导通后特性近似竖直，因此小信号等效有两个状态：关断时开路，导通时近似短路。

method.method_draft: Let all resistors be R = 2 kΩ. In the incremental circuit, put conductance G = 1/R for each resistor and diode conductance g_d between Vout node A and right node B. Write KCL: G(v_A-v_in)+(G+g_d)(v_A-v_B)=0 and Gv_B+(G+g_d)(v_B-v_A)=0. Solve these two equations to get A_v = v_A/v_in = (2+x)/(3+2x), where x = g_d/G. From the diode plot, off state gives x=0, so A_v=2/3; on state gives x→∞, so A_v→1/2. Therefore the ratio of minimum to maximum gain is (1/2)/(2/3)=0.75.
